title: Only multilayer perceptrons explored for G and D
description: The paper only explores the special case where both the generative model and discriminative model are multilayer perceptrons, leaving other model classes and optimization algorithms for future work.
canonical_description: generative and discriminative models limited to multilayer perceptron architecture

verdict.reasoning: No candidate papers were deep-read, so there is no evidence the gap has been addressed.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: Highly tractable. Data is abundant (CIFAR, ImageNet, CelebA, etc.) and freely available. Compute is modest — training a GAN with different architectures (CNNs, ResNets, Transformers) fits on a single GPU, far from frontier-scale pretraining. Methodological maturity is high: backpropagation, GAN training dynamics, and architectural building blocks (convolutions, attention, normalization layers) are well understood, so this is an engineering/architecture search problem, not a fundamental breakthrough. Scope is focused (swap the G/D backbone, train, evaluate). Evaluation is clear via Inception Score, FID, and visual inspection. The only reason it is not a 1.0 is that the gap, as literally stated, is extremely broad — the researcher must decide which architecture family to try and on which task, and the space of possibilities is large. But any single concrete instantiation (e.g., "replace MLP with a ResNet generator") is straightforward to execute and measure.
